subject: AeroNova RFP — clarifications on indemnity, IP and order form
messages:
From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@aeronova.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@aeronova.com>, procurement@aeronova.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP legal clarifications / order form draft

Jonas —

Thanks for the RFP responses so far. Our legal team has a couple of follow-ups on the liability and IP sections in the template you provided, and we've attached a draft order form for your review. High-level items we need clarity on:

- Indemnity: your RFP shows Redwood offering Customer->Redwood indemnity for data breaches, but AeroNova requires a reciprocal IP infringement indemnity for third-party claims arising from the service. Are you willing to accept an IP indemnity carve-out?
- Liability cap: RFP suggests a cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months. AeroNova needs to understand if you have any exceptions (e.g., willful misconduct, IP indemnity).
- IP assignment / rights: Section on derived model improvements is a bit vague. We need confirmation that AeroNova retains ownership of our input data and that Redwood does not claim assignment of customer-trained models.
- Order form: the draft we attached includes net-60 payment terms and an annual subscription. If you need different billing cadence or auto-renewal language, let us know.

Could you confirm Redwood's positions or propose alternate language? If it's easier, we can hop on a short call this week.

Thanks,

Sarah Jennings
Senior Counsel, Contracts
AeroNova Technologies

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and for sending the order form. Looping in our legal lead (Mina) and CS/programs (Evelyn) so we can get you definitive language.

High-level from me: Redwood typically offers a narrow IP infringement indemnity limited to direct infringement by our service (not customer content). Our commercial liability cap is normally the greater of 12 months fees or $1,000,000, with statutory carve-outs for fraud/willful misconduct. We do not claim assignment of customer data or customer models — customers retain their input data and any access-based artifacts.

I've asked Mina to provide redlines and the standard positions we propose for AeroNova. We can then either mark up your order form or provide a one-page addendum.

I'll also flag billing: your draft shows net-60; our standard for enterprise pilots is net-45, but that's negotiable.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP legal clarifications / order form draft — proposed redlines

Jonas / Evelyn —

Thanks for the loop. Sarah — copying you on our proposed positions below and attaching a redline for the RFP sections you flagged (Redwood_RFP_Response_Redline.pdf) and a companion doc with explanations (Redwood_RFP_Response_IP_Indemnity.docx). Key points: 

1) IP Indemnity
- Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that the hosted service, provided under the Agreement, directly infringes a third party's issued U.S. patent, copyright or trade secret ("IP Indemnity").
- Conditions: Customer must (i) notify Redwood promptly of the claim; (ii) allow Redwood to control defense/settlement; and (iii) provide reasonable cooperation.
- Limitation: Redwood's IP Indemnity does not extend to (a) Customer Content that causes infringement; (b) modifications made by Customer or a third party; or (c) models fine-tuned by Customer on Customer data.

2) Liability Cap
- Redwood's general liability cap = the greater of (a) fees paid to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the event, or (b) USD 1,000,000.
- Carve-outs: No cap for liability arising from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality affecting regulated data, or (iii) Redwood's indemnity obligations under Section X (IP Indemnity).

3) IP / Ownership
- Customer Content: Customers retain ownership of their input data and outputs generated from that data. Redwood only obtains a limited license to process Customer Content for providing the Service and operating/improving the Service (see limited terms below).
- Model Improvements: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and performance data to improve the service. Redwood will not claim assignment of customer-trained models or assert ownership over any models that are solely derived from Customer-provided weights or training artifacts.
- Optional add-on: for customers requiring stronger guarantees, we can propose a scoped data isolation addendum or a private deployment (Redwood Private) where telemetry/aggregates are opt-out.

4) Order Form / Payment Terms
- Standard payment: net-45 for enterprise subscriptions; net-60 is acceptable for larger enterprise accounts with a purchase order on file.
- Auto-renewal: 1-year term with automatic renewal unless either party provides written notice 60 days prior to renewal.
- Early termination: refunds are pro-rated for pre-paid annual subscriptions; termination for convenience is not standard but can be negotiated for strategic customers.

Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Response_Redline.pdf (redline of RFP & order form), Redwood_RFP_Response_IP_Indemnity.docx (explanatory note).

If AeroNova needs stronger IP remedies or a separate assignment carve-out, please let us know specifics and we will escalate. Happy to schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call this week.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Head of Legal — Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Sarah / AeroNova team —

Thanks for raising these items. Attaching our redlined response (Redwood_RFP_Response_Redline.pdf) which includes the language Mina summarized below. Short answers up front:

- IP Indemnity: Redwood will provide a limited IP infringement indemnity for the Service itself, with standard notice/cooperation requirements and exclusions for customer content/modifications.
- Liability cap: Our cap is the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000; carve-outs as described by Mina (fraud/willful misconduct and IP indemnity) apply.
- Ownership: AeroNova retains your input data and outputs; Redwood will not claim assignment of customer-trained models. We may use aggregated/de-identified telemetry to improve the service.
- Order form: We can accept net-60 where required; our standard is net-45. We propose a 1-year initial term, auto-renew unless 60 days notice.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached redline.
2) If the redline is acceptable, we can (a) incorporate these changes into the order form and issue a clean copy, or (b) set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to agree final language.

Would Thursday 10–10:30am PT work for your counsel? If not, propose two alternate times.

Looking forward —

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
